item.text: I’m keeping the refactor inside SQL completion again. The next step is to extract the completion-engine selection policy itself, because UI and LSP still decide between legacy and semantic analyzers differently.

I confirmed the inconsistency: UI uses mode plus capability gating plus legacy fallback, while LSP still does a simple mode check. I’m extracting that policy into a shared SQL-model decision object so both callers get the same behavior surface.

item.text: I’m making the selection policy explicit now instead of leaving it implicit in booleans. The shared helper will encode when semantic completion is actually available and when legacy completion should be used as a fallback, then both UI and LSP will consume that same decision.

I caught one bad edge while wiring the shared decider into LSP: resolving with no data source would suppress the intended legacy fallback. I’m fixing that to pass the actual document data source through the decision path.

The other design issue is `COMBINED`: LSP was still effectively single-engine. I’m aligning it with the shared decision model so it can collect semantic proposals when available and also include legacy proposals when the mode allows or when semantic can’t run.
The shared decider is in; now I’m cleaning the callers and adding focused tests for the decision rules so this isn’t just a code move.

Plan:
1. Extract a shared completion-engine decision policy into `model.sql`.
2. Replace UI and LSP-specific analyzer-selection logic with that shared policy.
3. Add focused model-layer tests for the shared decision rules and sanity-check the touched files.
